ca-sb100.bill: The 100 Percent Clean Energy Act of 2018
ca-sb100.leverage_point: Residents can advocate for local renewable energy projects, monitor utility compliance, and participate in city council or utility board meetings to push for faster adoption of clean energy.
ca-sb100.summary: SB 100 requires California to achieve 100% clean, zero-carbon electricity by 2045, mandating utilities and local governments to plan for and implement renewable energy procurement and grid integration.

ca-ab1279.leverage_point: Residents can use this law to demand local climate action plans align with state targets and to advocate for emissions reduction measures in city and county planning processes.
ca-ab1279.summary: AB 1279 establishes a statewide goal for California to achieve net zero greenhouse gas emissions as soon as possible, but no later than 2045, and to achieve and maintain net negative emissions thereafter.

ca-sb1053.leverage_point: Residents can report non-compliant retailers to local authorities and participate in city meetings to ensure robust enforcement and public outreach.
ca-sb1053.summary: SB 1053 bans all plastic bags at retail checkout, allowing only paper bags with a fee, and requires local governments to enforce the ban and educate retailers and the public.

ca-ab130.bill: CEQA Infill Housing and Streamlining Reform
ca-ab130.leverage_point: Residents can participate in local hearings to ensure transparency, advocate for equitable infill development, and monitor the use of CEQA exemptions in their neighborhoods.
ca-ab130.summary: AB 130 creates a CEQA exemption for qualifying infill housing and expands streamlining provisions, requiring local governments to update permitting processes and provide public notice for eligible projects.

ca-sb131.bill: CEQA Exemptions for Infrastructure and Climate Resilience Projects
ca-sb131.leverage_point: Residents can monitor local project proposals, demand public notice and transparency, and advocate for environmental justice in the application of exemptions.
ca-sb131.summary: SB 131 introduces broad CEQA exemptions for infrastructure, community-serving facilities, and climate resilience projects, requiring local governments to implement new review procedures and limiting public hearings.
